Chapter 3: Replacing Old Stories with New Truths.
Once you’ve spotted the lies you’ve been telling yourself, there’s one more big step—finding something stronger to take their place. It’s not enough to just push those old beliefs aside. Your mind craves new stories to fill that empty space. For a lot of us, that’s where faith steps in and becomes a lifeline.
There’s this woman I know of, who spent years feeling invisible. Then, she started wondering what it might mean to be truly seen by God. Up until then, she’d always thought her value depended on what other people thought of her. But as she read stories from scripture—stories about people who were left out, dismissed, or even broken—she started to notice a pattern. Time after time, the ones who seemed least important were actually chosen, loved, and given real purpose.
Now, realizing this didn’t magically erase all her doubts overnight. But it did give her a new foundation to stand on. She stopped measuring herself by everyone else’s shifting standards and began anchoring her identity in something that doesn’t change. The idea that worth is given, not earned—that became a quiet, steady source of strength.
Then there’s someone else, weighed down by regrets from her past, who struggled to believe she could ever change. The old story in her head went, “You’ll always be this way.” But as she reflected on the idea of grace, things started to shift. The possibility of forgiveness, and the hope of a fresh start, opened a door she never even realized was there.
Most of us find that swapping out our old stories is a slow, gentle process—not just about thinking positive or repeating nice affirmations. It’s about coming back, again and again, to truths that actually bring hope. For people who lean on faith, this often means soaking in scripture—not as a rulebook, but as a collection of reminders about who you really are, and what could be possible.
There’s a quiet power in this practice. Over time, these new stories start to feel more familiar. The old lies just don’t grip as tightly. You’ll catch those negative thoughts creeping in, and now you’ve got something truer to say back. Instead of “I’m not enough,” you’ll start to believe, “I am loved, just as I am.” Instead of “I’ll never change,” you’ll find yourself saying, “Growth is possible—even for me.”
Remember, this isn’t about pretending pain doesn’t exist, or ignoring the tough stuff. It’s about choosing which stories you’ll let shape your future. And most people discover, the more they return to these new truths, the more confident and free they begin to feel. The journey isn’t a straight line—there’ll be setbacks, doubts, and hard days. But with every step, the old scripts lose a little more power, and these new, life-giving stories start to take root.
